question.problem: Given that $p(x)=3{x}^{2}$ and $q(x)=5{x}^{7},$ what is ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }(p(x)\cdot q(x))?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply the two functions, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }(p(x)\cdot q(x)) & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(3{x}^{2}\cdot 5{x}^{7}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }((3\cdot 5){x}^{2+7}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(15\cdot {x}^{9}) \\  & =15\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{9}\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y={x}^{9}$ is power function with an odd positive power and therefore has the property that

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{9}=-\infty .
$$

Multiplication by the positive constant $15$ does not affect the limit at infinity. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}15\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{9}={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{9}=-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }(15{x}^{9})=-\infty .
$$
